BiblicalUsage: Ratson is delight — favour, goodwill, pleasure, and by extension, the will of God. The psalm says, 'For thou, LORD, wilt bless the righteous; with favour wilt thou compass him as with a shield'; and again, 'I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart'; the Proverb says, 'whoso findeth me findeth life, and shall obtain favour of the LORD'; and Isaiah proclaims 'the acceptable year of the LORD.'
TheologicalSignificance: I take it that favour is God's shield around the righteous: He compasses them with goodwill, and His will is not a burden but a delight. And my position is that the acceptable year is still open — the LORD's favour is proclaimed, and the day of His vengeance waits behind it.
